content:
One of the most frustrating aspects of the iPhone user interface is that we have to play a guessing game just to change an app's settings.

Sometimes we'll open the app itself and go into its built-in settings menu. But other times we have to leave the app and open a completely separate Apple "Settings" app. This experience, frankly, is quite clumsy (though there's a free shortcut that can help)...

The "Settings" Problem

We've all experienced this. You want to change an app's setting, so you go to the "hamburger menu," select "Settings," and look for what you want to change. You can't find it, only to realize you have to leave the app, open Apple's "Settings" app, find that app, make your change there, and then finally reopen the app you wanted to use in the first place.

The process itself is already clumsy, but what's even worse is that at the very beginning we have to guess where to look.

Take Apple's "Camera" app as an example. Recent iPhones provide what Apple calls a "Fusion Camera" for the 1x lens. The default is 24mm, but we can actually change the default to 28mm or 35mm. The way it works is that the app automatically applies a crop effect. Additionally, we can also choose whether or not we have to tap the "1x" button to cycle through different focal lengths.

However, unless it's hidden somewhere I haven't discovered, there's no way to do this directly within the "Camera" app. Instead, we have to open the "Settings" app, find "Camera"*, scroll down to the "Photo Capture" section, tap "Fusion Camera"—only then do we get to where we can make our selection.

*And I haven't even mentioned another thing: you also have to guess whether an Apple app will have its own dedicated section in "Settings" or get lumped into the "Apps" section...

Using a Shortcut as a Partial Workaround

There's no way to completely avoid the guessing game, but at least there's a third-party shortcut created by Quinn Nelson at Snazzy Labs that can help reduce some of the pain.

Thanks to John Gruber for bringing this shortcut to my attention. If you'd like to install it yourself:

  • Download and install it here
  • Open "Control Center"
  • Tap the + button in the top-left corner
  • Tap "Add a Control" at the bottom
  • Search for "Shortcuts"
  • Tap "Run Shortcut"
  • Select the "App Settings" shortcut

Once installed, if you're using an app and find that you need to go to the separate "Settings" app to find a setting, just swipe down from the top-right corner to open "Control Center," then tap the "App Settings" button.

However, Apple Should Properly Fix This Problem

What I'd love to see is a comprehensive fix, not reliance on third-party workarounds.

My suggestion is that there should be a "More" option at the bottom of every app's settings menu that automatically opens the "Settings" app and jumps to the correct page. That way, if we can't find what we're looking for in the app's internal settings menu, it's just one more tap.

To be clear, Apple already provides an API that can do this, but not many developers use it. I hope Apple can make this a mandatory requirement.

Is there anything you'd like to see? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
